prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the camera wearer's forward movement from a hallway about 1.5–2.5 metres outside an open bathroom doorway in frame 1, passing directly through the bright, arm's-reach door frame (under 0.5 metres on the left and right edges) in frame 2, and advancing into the bathroom toward the right-hand vanity wall across frames 3 to 5. Inside the bathroom, the recessed shower alcove with its high curtain rod, left-wall caddy, and hanging mesh bag lies furthest away at roughly 1.5–2.5 metres in the upper-left background, while the sink and the small child positioned just in front of and below the basin appear as nearer mid-grey shapes at the bottom edge, closing from about 1.5 metres in frame 2 to within arm's reach (0.5–1.0 metres) in frames 3 and 4 before dropping mostly out of view in frame 5. The map clarifies the continuous planar gradient of the right wall and doorway relative to the recessed shower enclosure better than the flatly lit yellow RGB images. However, the depth map is unreliable on the right-wall mirror in frames 3 to 5, rendering the mirror as a flat, near surface (0.5–1.0 metres away) and completely missing the virtual depth of the reflected room, the child's reflection, and the camera wearer's own reflection.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map detects only three isolated regions across the five frames: the bathroom sink at the bottom-centre of frame 2 (roughly 1.5 metres ahead and below camera level, about 0.5 metres below the mirror) and the camera wearer's own reflection entering the right-hand mirror in frames 4 and 5 (at an apparent optical distance of 1.0–1.5 metres to the right). As the camera wearer steps forward and turns slightly right toward the vanity across the sequence, the sink mask drops below the lower frame boundary after frame 2 while the reflected figure enters from the right edge in frame 4 (within arm's reach of the physical mirror surface) and becomes more fully visible from the thighs up in frame 5. While the masks sharply delineate the curved basin rim in frame 2 and the silhouette of the reflected body in frames 4 and 5, the map is largely unreliable for scene understanding. It mislabels the partially occluded reflection of the camera wearer at the right border of frame 4 as a 'cat', treats the mirror reflection in frame 5 as a real 'person' standing in front of the camera, and completely misses the real small child at the bottom of frames 2 to 4 as well as the shower curtain, rod, wall caddy, and doorway.
descriptions.pose: The pose map extracts 2D body skeletons in only two frames, showing a small, fragmented yellow skeleton at the sink in the bottom-centre of frame 2 (about 1.5 metres away) and a larger torso-and-arms skeleton on the far right in frame 5 (representing the camera wearer's mirror reflection at an apparent distance of about 1.0–1.5 metres). In frame 2, the tiny keypoints on the child near the sink basin indicate a body positioned low and within arm's reach of the sink rim, mostly cropped by the bottom edge of the frame and facing roughly toward the sink and mirror. In frame 5, the reflected upper-body skeleton shows shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips, and head keypoints oriented sideways and angled toward the mirror and sink (so the reflection faces left and slightly toward the camera viewpoint), with both arms hanging down within reach of the vanity counter and about 0.3–0.5 metres above the child's reflected head. Although pose estimation makes the articulated limb positions of the blurred reflection in frame 5 much clearer than in the RGB image, it is unreliable across the sequence because it fails to detect the child in frames 3 and 4, misses the partially visible reflection in frame 4, registers no magenta hand skeletons in any frame, and treats a 2D mirror reflection as a person in 3D space.
